description: That figure is down from 17 vessels on Wednesday and falls below the 10-day average of around 15 vessels. description: Germany July import prices +0.2% m/m Prior -0.7% Germany July import prices +6.8% y/y Prior +6.1% Import prices in Germany continue to pick up, with the annual estimate now rising to 6.8%. title: What are the main events for today?
description: EUROPEAN SESSION In the European session, we get the preliminary inflation reports for France and Spain. They are both expected to rise given the increase in energy prices in August, but the focus will be on the core figures. Nevertheless, the ECB has already pre-committed to a rate hike in September and signalled that there's less appetite to tighter further afterwards, so the market reaction might be muted, as the data won't change anything for near-term policy. title: France August preliminary CPI +2.4% vs +2.4% y/y expected
description: Prior +2.1% HICP +2.7% vs +2.6% y/y expected Prior +2.4% French inflation picked up in August with stronger energy prices offsetting softer pressures from the services sector. The acceleration was primarily driven by energy costs, particularly petroleum products, which increased at a faster pace than in the previous month. Food prices also contributed modestly to the uptick in inflation, while the decline in manufactured goods prices continued to ease. title: France Q2 final GDP +0.0% vs +0.2% q/q prelim
description: Prior -0.2% GDP Y/Y +0.5% vs +0.7 expected Prior +0.9% France's economy stagnated in the second quarter of 2026, with real GDP unchanged from the previous quarter after contracting 0.2% in Q1. While a sharp rebound in exports helped stabilize growth, household purchasing power weakened further and savings fell markedly as inflation accelerated. Household consumption returned to growth during the quarter, rising 0.3% after a 0.3% decline in Q1. title: Spain August preliminary CPI +4.3% vs +4.2% y/y expected
description: Prior +3.6% HICP +4.5% vs +4.6% y/y expected Prior +3.9% Core CPI Y/Y +2.9% vs +3.0% prior Spain's annual inflation rate accelerated sharply in August, with rising fuel costs pushing headline inflation to its highest level in more than a year. The main factor behind the acceleration was the fuel and lubricants component, where prices increased compared with declines recorded in August 2025. The comparison with last year's weakness in energy prices generated a significant upward base effect, making fuel costs the largest contributor to the rise in headline inflation.
